# N038 diagnosis: where the gap (.67 - .6527 = .017) lives

## Ceiling test D1b (same architecture, identical cells) -- d1b_same_arch.py -> d1b_same_arch.csv
Same SSL encoder (n007 r50), same 10-epoch fine-tune; FOV-split model trained on BOTH draws (n015_sslinit_fov, i.e. it HAS seen the
test draw, 318k cells) vs batch-held-out single model (n023_v5_b10/b01, other draw only), scored on the SAME split-2 cells of the test
draw, v5 labels, common-11:
  draw 0 test: in-distribution .6552 vs held-out .6437 (gap .0115); draw 1 test: .6612 vs .6409 (gap .0203); overall .6582 vs .6423.
D1 (n024 r18 FOV vs the N031 GOAL ensemble, same cells): r18 in-distribution .6457/.6741 vs ensemble .6612/.6443 (d1_fov_vs_batch.csv).
=> Seeing the test draw is worth ~.016 for the current model family. A PERFECT removal of the draw shift (single model) would land at
~.658; with the +.010 ensemble gain at ~.668 -- i.e. the target .67 sits AT the in-distribution ceiling of the current predictor.
The "FOV ~.71 vs batch .634" gap quoted in GOAL target_source compared different cell/target sets; on identical cells it is ~.016.

## Where the mean is lost (per target, D1b in-distribution / held-out)
Lineage markers are at their ceiling with ~0 shift cost: CD14 .85-.88, CD16 .89-.91, CD45 .71-.88, grp:CD3/19/56 .77-.79.
Four targets drag the mean, in-distribution too: CD19 .28/.47, CD56 .41/.39, CD123 .41/.53, HLA-DR .61/.60 (held-out .28-.56).
Raising each of these four by +.10 would add ~+.036 to the 11-target mean (= 2x the gap); the draw shift is concentrated in the same
targets (HLA-DR +.05/.15, CD19 .00/.10, CD56 .05/.01) plus grp:CD45 draw 0 (.125).

## Bottleneck hypothesis
The GOAL is bounded by PER-CELL information about lymphoid subsets and rare/dim populations (CD19 B cells, CD56 NK, CD123
basophils/pDC, HLA-DR on monocytes/B) -- either (a) image-limited: 128-px single-cell LF crops at the current resolution / model do
not resolve them, or (b) label-limited: dim antibodies, autofluorescence-dominated unmixing and the position artefact (K007: position
alone predicts CD19 .84) leave low label reliability. Both cap in-distribution r, so neither draw-shift work (DANN, AdaBN refuted)
nor training-label hygiene (N037 flat) can reach .67. Evidence for (b): N035 post-hoc, the label of CD19 is only r .32 (draw 0) /
.56 (draw 1) predictable from the cell's own fluorescence integrals (FOV-CV ridge), CD56 .54/.48, vs CD16 .97 (label mostly NOT the
cell's own photons after detrend+unmixing); K004 within-class r .08-.45; K020 tail/focal helps in-distribution only.

## What would falsify it
1. Label reliability ceiling: a spectral split-half (or bimodality/mixture) reliability estimate for CD19/CD56/CD123/HLA-DR labels
   >= .85 => labels are reliable, the image model is the bottleneck (then resolution/context/model changes are the lever).
   Reliability <= r^2-compatible (sqrt(rel) ~ current in-distribution r) => the GOAL target is unreachable and must be re-scoped.
2. An in-distribution model with much more information (full LED stack at native resolution, larger context, larger backbone)
   reaching >> .66 on the same FOV cells => the current predictor, not the data, is the ceiling.
3. If the draw-shift part (.016) closes with a method that never sees test-draw images in training (GOAL constraint is inductive:
   no test-draw images in pretraining; treat self-training on test images as transductive and report it only as a control),
   e.g. physics-based LED/illumination augmentation or draw-invariant input normalisation, the GOAL reaches ~.668.
Metric is not the limit: noise .002 vs gap .017.

Protocols: fov (train split 0 / eval split 2, both batches) | b1to0 (train batch 1, eval batch-0 test FOVs) | b0to1.

import sys, os; sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from bsccm.data import chan_list, W
from bsccm.gpu_norm import RawSet, GPUNorm
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--out', required=True); ap.add_argument('--protocol', default='fov'); ap.add_argument('--channels', default='all')
ap.add_argument('--phase', type=int, default=1); ap.add_argument('--arch', default='resnet18'); ap.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=8)
ap.add_argument('--bs', type=int, default=256); ap.add_argument('--lr', type=float, default=1e-3); ap.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=15)
ap.add_argument('--max-train', type=int, default=0); ap.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=0); ap.add_argument('--w-cls', type=float, default=0.5); ap.add_argument('--include-gs', type=int, default=0)
ap.add_argument('--init-ssl', default=''); ap.add_argument('--tail-weight', type=float, default=0.0); ap.add_argument('--focal-c10', type=float, default=0.0); ap.add_argument('--targets', default='targets_v4.npz'); ap.add_argument('--dann', type=float, default=0.0)
ap.add_argument('--stem', default='std', choices=['std', 'nomaxpool']); ap.add_argument('--zoom', type=int, default=1)   # N026 resolution: centre crop 128/zoom -> upsample to 128
ap.add_argument('--dual-zoom', type=int, default=1)   # N026: shared encoder sees full view AND centre-zoom view; features concatenated
ap.add_argument('--adabn', type=int, default=0)   # N026: after training, recompute BN stats on N unlabelled target-batch images (split 0), evaluate again
a = ap.parse_args(); os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True); torch.manual_seed(a.seed); np.random.seed(a.seed)
T = np.load(W + '/' + a.targets); names = list(T['names']); K = len(names)
Y, Mk, c3, c10, sp, b = T['Y'], T['mask'], T['cls3'], T['cls10'], T['split'], T['batch']
has = Mk.any(1) | (c3 >= 0)
if not a.include_gs: has &= T['hist_row'] < 0   # keep the 15,712 GS cells (label: autofl only) out of LF training -> clean GS autofl test
if a.protocol == 'fov': tr = (sp == 0) & has; ev = (sp == 2) & has
elif a.protocol == 'b1to0': tr = (b == 1) & has; ev = (b == 0) & (sp == 2) & has
elif a.protocol == 'b0to1': tr = (b == 0) & has; ev = (b == 1) & (sp == 2) & has
else: raise SystemExit('protocol?')
tr, ev = np.where(tr)[0], np.where(ev)[0]
if a.max_train: tr = np.random.default_rng(0).permutation(tr)[:a.max_train]
print(f'train {len(tr)} eval {len(ev)} protocol {a.protocol}', flush=True)
nin = len(chan_list(a.channels)) + a.phase
Wt_ = np.ones(Y.shape, np.float32)
if a.tail_weight > 0:   # fine-grained: up-weight rare marker values (density^-alpha in 60 bins over [-4, 4], per batch x target, clipped [.2, 10], mean 1)
    edges = np.linspace(-4, 4, 61)
    for j in range(K):
        for bb in (0, 1):
            m_tr = np.zeros(len(Y), bool); m_tr[tr] = True; sel = m_tr & Mk[:, j] & (b == bb)
            if sel.sum() < 100: continue
            h, _ = np.histogram(np.clip(Y[sel, j], -4, 4), edges); dens = (h + 1) / (h.sum() + len(h))
            allsel = Mk[:, j] & (b == bb); idx = np.clip(np.digitize(np.clip(Y[allsel, j], -4, 4), edges) - 1, 0, 59)
            w = np.clip(dens[idx] ** (-a.tail_weight), 0.2, 10.0); w = w / w[m_tr[allsel]].mean(); Wt_[allsel, j] = w
LAB = {'Y': Y, 'M': Mk, 'c3': c3.astype(np.int64), 'c10': c10.astype(np.int64), 'W': Wt_}
mk = lambda rows, train: torch.utils.data.DataLoader(RawSet(rows, LAB), batch_size=a.bs, shuffle=train, drop_last=train,

_cnt = np.bincount(c10[tr][c10[tr] >= 0], minlength=10).astype(np.float32); C10W = torch.tensor(1 / np.sqrt(np.maximum(_cnt, 1)), device='cuda'); C10W = C10W / C10W[_cnt > 0].mean()
def prep(raw, ph, g, train):   # raw int16 records -> normalised LF on GPU (+-4 px translation when training)
    x = gnorm(raw.cuda(non_blocking=True), ph.cuda(non_blocking=True), g.cuda(non_blocking=True), CH, bool(a.phase), shift=4 if train else 0)
    if a.zoom > 1:

sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(opt, a.lr, total_steps=steps, pct_start=0.1)
class _GRL(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x, l): ctx.l = l; return x.view_as(x)
    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, g): return -ctx.l * g, None

    if SSL: x = torch.cat([x, torch.ones_like(x)], 1)

            h = torch.cat([h, model['enc'](xz.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last))], 1)
    h = h.float(); return model['reg'](h), model['c3'](h), model['c10'](h), h
def pearson(p, y):
    p, y = p - p.mean(), y - y.mean(); return float((p * y).sum() / (np.sqrt((p * p).sum() * (y * y).sum()) + 1e-9))
@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate(save=False, tag=''):
    model.eval(); P, C3, G = [], [], []
    C10 = []
    for raw, ph, g, y, m, k3, k10, _w in dev:

    P, C3, G = np.concatenate(P), np.concatenate(C3), np.concatenate(G); Yt, Mt, k3 = Y[G], Mk[G], c3[G]; r = {}
    for j, n in enumerate(names):

    lab = k3 >= 0

        for j in range(8, 12):   # pooled groups on gated cells: within-class r + class-oracle baseline
            v = lab & Mt[:, j]

            r[f'oracle_classmean_r/{names[j]}'] = pearson(oracle, Yt[v, j]); r[f'r_gated/{names[j]}'] = pearson(P[v, j], Yt[v, j])
            for k, kn in enumerate(['lym', 'gran', 'mono']):
                vk = v & (k3 == k)

    r['r_mean_markers'] = float(np.mean([r[f'r/{n}'] for n in names[:12] if f'r/{n}' in r]))

    r['r_mean_markers_valid'] = float(np.mean([r[f'r/{n}'] for j, n in enumerate(names[:12]) if f'r/{n}' in r and trained[j]]))

But two fixed draws, one FOV partition, and one trained instance per D1b arm cannot bound performance on a future isolation, another split, or other recipes. The contrast combines access to target-draw labels, source/target composition, sample count, loss targets, and optimizer updates. It is not an intervention that removes only draw shift.
3. **Both D1b arms are transductive in SSL.** n007's saved configuration says `rows='all'`, `exclude_batch=[]`, `n_rows=412941`. Even the “held-out” D1b model has seen target-draw images during SSL, including evaluation images. That is compatible with a transductive diagnostic control, but fails the inductive GOAL constraint. N031 instead uses encoders excluding the held-out draw. Reproduced N031 scores confirm the GOAL .652741; they do not make D1b an inductive causal comparison. Nor does this evidence establish that transduction explains away the scores: the recorded N031 aggregate control was essentially flat.
4. **The evaluation is split 2 only.** N015 has 39,435 unique non-Giemsa evaluation cells: 13,113 from draw 0 and 26,322 from draw 1. These are precisely the batch-model evaluation cohorts, so there is no hidden cell mismatch here. But two fixed draws, one FOV partition, and one trained instance per D1b arm cannot bound performance on a future isolation, another split, or other recipes. The .002 seed-noise estimate is not a population-level confidence bound on an information ceiling.

The D1b summary is a **net score difference**, with substantial cancellation:

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| common-11 | +.011541 | +.020296 | +.015918 |

In draw 1 alone, grp:CD3/CD19/CD56 and grp:CD16 have gaps −.106418 and −.087848. This cancellation cannot justify “draw shift costs only .016.” Conversely, the unchanged-label single-target subset does not cleanly identify shift either, because training size and the multi-output training objective still differ.

## Existing counterexample to .658

Using the same cells and the actual v5 common-11 metric:

| FOV model | Draw 0 | Draw 1 | Equal-draw mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| N015 SSL-init R50 | .655198 | .661177 | .658188 |
| N022 base R50 | .657514 | .660203 | .658859 |
| **N022 tail05 R50** | **.686617** | **.673334** | **.679976** |
| N024 supervised R18, v5-trained | .645697 | .674081 | .659889 |

N022 tail05 retains the SSL-init R50, 128-pixel input recipe, and v4 training labels; it changes tail weighting and the focal class head. Its evaluation-row array is exactly equal to N015's. It beats N015 by .021788 under the diagnosis's own evaluation conditions, without new image information. This is stronger evidence against a family-wide ceiling than an architecture mismatch. Its previously reported failure to improve held-out b1to0 remains compatible with this finding: **an in-distribution capacity/training result and generalization to a new draw are different questions.**

For uncertainty, a paired bootstrap resampled slide/FOV clusters within each draw, with equal weighting of draw means (1,000 replicates, seed 20261112). The 95% percentile interval for tail05 minus N015 is [.011940, .028988]. N015's mean interval is [.646425, .670094]; tail05's is [.663999, .693722]. These are conditional intervals for these trained models and these draws, with no adjustment for historical model selection. They reject treating .658 as an exact limit; they do not prove a population score above .67. The paired overall D1b gap interval is [.005498, .028719], describing that confounded contrast only.

The old “FOV ~.71 versus batch .634” numbers should indeed not be interpreted as a controlled shift experiment. Replacing them with a differently confounded .016 comparison does not solve that problem.

## Are the four dim-target conclusions robust?

Only the descriptive statement that several targets are weaker than CD14/CD16 is robust. The four do not exhibit one common failure mechanism.

| CD19 | .279 / .467 | .280 / .365 | .325 / .437 | Weak and draw-dependent; draw-0 shift effect near zero, draw-1 positive |

| CD123 | .408 / .528 | .555 / .461 | **.646 / .676** | Strong sensitivity to training objective; low N015 score is not an information bound |

The currently compliant N031 ensemble already reaches CD123 .614830 on draw 0, above N015's purported in-distribution reference .407966. N024's CD123 reference is weaker still (.304377/.399814). Calling those references a ceiling is empirically backwards for that target.

HLA-DR's D1b FOV-minus-batch gaps are +.054284/+.145156. The paired FOV bootstrap intervals are [.024866, .083515] and [.113254, .177785]. Both are positive in this conditional comparison; the cause remains confounded. CD19 and CD56 gaps vary by draw; CD123 gap intervals span zero in both draws. A uniform “four dim targets are capped” conclusion therefore exceeds the evidence.

HLA-DR is not even the fourth-lowest N015 target by draw-averaged correlation: single CD3 is .584988 versus HLA-DR .606430. Statements that high-scoring lineage markers are “at their ceiling” are also **[unverified]** without an independent upper-bound estimate. Adding .10 to any four targets would increase the 11-target mean by .03636; that arithmetic does not identify a mechanism or achievable intervention.

They are not technical replicate reliability estimates, nor the same split-2 v5 test. A low score for a restricted linear readout can reflect missing spatial/position-correction information, nonlinear relationships, or cross-FOV transfer; it does not show that the curated label mostly lacks the cell's photons. **[Unverified]** Image-information limits, independent measurement-noise ceilings, and irreducibility of any particular target remain hypotheses. Neither dimness nor a low trained-model correlation identifies which applies. The attenuation bound `r <= sqrt(reliability)` requires a suitable measurement-error model and an independently valid reliability estimate. Bimodality alone is not such an estimate; spectral halves require justified independence and comparability.
